findings.where: the 'overwhelmed' feeling as it lands, lower half of the frame, frames 336-392 (5.38-6.27 s of app time at 16 ms a step); worst at frame 339

findings.what: the check written to find flat fills reads only the ten stills and never opens a frame of any clip, which is where both fills above are: it reports files_with_a_flat_fill 0 and sheets_with_no_paper_on_them [] for every still, and separately the scene reports say sheets_on_the_glass_with_no_paper_on_them {"sticky_blue_02": 2} in 01_pulse, 03_us, 05_settings, 06_unfolding, 11_chat_scroll, 13_messenger_states and 14_media_viewer, {"sticky_blue_02": 2, "graph_03": 1} in 12_search and {"sticky_blue_02_dusk": 3} in dusk_pulse - eight of thirteen scenes - while flat.json's list for the same stills is empty; I could find no flat blue sheet in any of them (largest pale-blue connected component in 01/03/05/12/13 is under 3,000 px and none of them flat), so the two records disagree and nothing in the set says which is right

findings.what: there is no picture of the Android app anywhere in the set, so none of the four anti-goals can be checked on an Android surface at all; the reason given is measured rather than asserted (no /dev/kvm, the x86_64 image under QEMU instruction emulation, adbd answering after 113 minutes with the framework never coming up behind it) and all fifteen artifacts that are present are from this run
findings.why: an Android app is half the mission's delivery target and my row says 'anywhere in the build'; the reason is a reason and not an excuse, but the consequence is that half of it is unexamined for this row and the score has to say so

what_is_working: No product-marketing voice in anything I could read. Across the 568 captured literals the only '!' characters are six Dart null-assertion operators inside interpolations (material/paper.dart:382 and :481, modules/calendar/calendar_module.dart:191, modules/shelf/shelf_module.dart:203, regions/chat/blob_widgets.dart:399, regions/chat/chat_region.dart:1145), none of which reaches the glass as a mark; zero matches for \buser, zero for love[ -]?tap|lovetap, zero for oops/whoops/yay/awesome/great job/welcome/get started/let's go/you're all set. On the glass the error path in 13_messenger_states.png reads 'it would not go X / send it again / this phone is on an older version and cannot read that', the empty states read 'nothing to do. suspicious.' and 'nowhere planned. that's fine.', and the pairing failure reads 'those aren't the words. try again.'

The app never names itself. logs/pwa.json reads the served manifest off the page and its name is 'the other phone'. 05_settings.png's first panel is headed 'THE TWO PHONES' and 17_setup_pwa.png's is 'this one, the iphone' - no product name appears in any of the ten stills or five clips.

Push, the one surface where marketing voice is almost universal, is bare. logs/reception.json's 24 shown records all use title 'noor' with bodies 'wrote something', 'is holding something out' and 'said how they are'; crops/reception.png shows exactly that on the glass; webpush.txt confirms the encrypted payload carries only ['kind','from'] in 32 bytes.

No emoji anywhere. My own detector over U+1F000-1FAFF, U+2600-27BF, U+2190-21FF, U+2B00-2BFF, U+FE0F and U+1F1E6-1F1FF found 0 across all 568 strings; logs/fonts.json bundles three hand fonts (DeskStamp 465 glyphs, NoorHand 775, TeoHand 775) and no emoji font; and I read all ten stills and stepped all five clips without one. The tick, cross and return marks on 13_messenger_states.png are pen strokes in the same hand and weight as the writing, and the compose row's magnifier and paperclip are drawn in that hand too. The single emoji in logs/tests.log is the Flutter tool's own root-warning banner, not app copy.

No stock illustration standing in for feeling. All 36 feelings in logs/haptics.json carry a named physical object (obj_pinch, obj_dog_ear, obj_crane, obj_mug, obj_plaster, obj_spitball, obj_scribble ...) and there is no heart, no smiley and no pictogram among them; logs/surfaces.json's objects_named_by_feelings puts 21 in `measured`, 10 in `read_but_not_measurable`, 5 in `drawn_in_the_app` and named_but_neither []. The picker in 15_authored_feeling.mp4 (frames 28-126) is six word-named families of rendered objects rather than a grid of glyphs, and the couple's own authored feeling is a pen drawing on a torn blue sticky whose flattest 24 px window measures 0.857 grey levels - real stock, not a fill.

No engagement machinery of any kind. 03_us.png's rituals row reads 'sunday 9 call - 20 times' (a tally of what happened: rituals_module.dart:126 '${r.marks.length} times'), to do reads '10 open · 16 done', the shelf reads '2 waiting on you · 6 between you', and 04_moments 'what happened' marks a kept ritual simply 'KEPT'. No badge, point, level, trophy, unlock, reward, streak-protection or guilt string appears in the 568 captured literals, and no numeric badge appears on any of the five tabs in any of the ten stills or five clips.

In the stills the paper is not simulated by any measure I took. Zero-variance connected regions in all ten stills top out at 391 px once the photograph in 14_media_viewer and the black video tile in 04_moments are set aside. Sheet silhouettes wander: top-edge rms 1.5-10.1 px with 13-53 px peak-to-peak over 587-792 columns in 02_chat, 01_pulse, 13_messenger_states and 17_setup_pwa, against 0.00 for a rounded rectangle. Paper tooth at 300 per cent autocorrelates 0.88 at lag 1, 0.52-0.58 at lag 4 and 0.05 by lag 16, so it is a resampled fibre field and not a per-pixel procedural overlay; the strongest repeat beyond lag 24 px is 0.089, so it is not tiled. The desk's strongest repeat beyond lag 64 px is 0.351 by day and 0.436 at dusk, at the grain-stripe spacing of 81 and 145 px rather than at a tile period. crops/02_chat_300_edge.png and _shadow.png show loose fibres standing off the tear at 300 per cent.

The narrowest places in the copy hold. The setup checklist in 17_setup_pwa.png is 'put this phone on the tailnet', 'install the profile the other phone is serving', 'add it to the home screen', 'read the six words off the other phone', 'let it interrupt you' - an onboarding flow with no welcome, no encouragement and no first-person-plural. 10_first_run.png reads 'nothing from them yet. the six words are on the other phone.' and 'first one's yours. whatever it is. it only goes to one person.'
verdict: Three of the four forbidden interpretations are not in this build, and not marginally: no emoji anywhere across ten stills, five clips, 568 captured strings and a font bundle with no emoji face in it; no stock illustration, because all 36 feelings are named physical objects with measured surfaces and the picker is six families of them rather than a grid of glyphs; and no product voice at all, with zero exclamation marks that reach the glass, zero uses of 'user', an installed manifest called 'the other phone', push bodies that say only 'wrote something', and a failed send that reads 'it would not go / send it again'. Engagement machinery is absent in the place it usually hides - the rituals surface counts '20 times' and marks a kept ritual 'KEPT', with no streak, no badge, no warning and no tab-bar number anywhere. The fourth interpretation is where the row loses its points, and only in the clips: at 5.42 s of app time in 07_feeling_landing the 'overwhelmed' feeling lands as a flat-shaded low-poly mesh carrying a single 33,389-pixel region of pure #FFFFFF at exactly zero local variance, a third of the screen of untextured geometry standing in for a crumpled sheet of paper, and its asset reads a tooth of 0.43 against the 0.45 the same file demands of paper - because logs/surfaces.json sets no tooth floor for the `objects` family at all, the one family the emotional layer is made of. A second flat fill, a beige rectangle of 10,507-12,297 px lying across the standing header, is on screen for 30-45 per cent of every clip that shows the Pulse header. Neither is visible in the ten stills, and logs/flat.json - the check written for exactly this - reports zero because it reads only stills. That is the finding holding this row below its floor: the paper system itself is genuinely photographic, so the concept is intact, but two surfaces on the glass are literally flat fills and one of them is the feeling itself.
not_worth_opening: evidence/SCORE.json and evidence/critics/13/ - another reader's conclusions, closed by the briefing and left closed.
evidence/reliability.json and evidence/coldstart.json - timing and flake records; nothing in them can carry a string, an emoji, a badge or a surface, so they cannot move this row.

evidence/logs/scroll_webkit.json and evidence/logs/11_chat_scroll.fling.json - per-frame build and raster cost and the thread's own fling record; a performance measurement, not a picture of anything an anti-goal names. I read 11_chat_scroll.mp4 itself instead.
evidence/logs/apk.json - a build record. It says nothing about what an Android screen shows, and no Android screen is in the set to check it against.

evidence/logs/<scene>.json (the per-step capture logs, as against the .report.json beside each) and evidence/scenes/*.json - the framing and the harness's wall-clock cost per step. I checked frames.json for the timebase and read the reports for what was on the glass; the step logs would not change what the pictures show.
evidence/logs/<clip>.frames.json and the two .sound.json files - held-frame accounting and audio; frames.json already carries the held-frame test for every clip and sound is outside this row.

evidence/.previous/ - the capture before this one. DIFF.json's labels were enough to confirm nothing in the set predates this run; comparing to an older build is the coherence critic's question, not this row's.

evidence/experiments/what_the_alternates_cost/ - I listed it and stopped. It is a cost comparison between two glyph-alternate settings, a performance trade, and neither branch of it can introduce one of the four interpretations.
